questions.q: What were the goals of India's Five Year Plans?
answer: After Independence India adopted economic planning through Five Year Plans, prepared by the Planning Commission set up in 1950, and these plans pursued four main goals.

answer.text: The first goal was growth, meaning an increase in the country's capacity to produce goods and services, so as to raise the standard of living and reduce poverty.
The second was modernisation, the adoption of new technology and improved methods of production, along with changes in social outlook such as granting women equal rights.
The third goal was self-reliance, avoiding dependence on imports of essential goods and foreign aid, so that the country could stand on its own feet, especially in food and industry.
The fourth goal was equity, ensuring that the benefits of growth reached all sections and that inequality and poverty were reduced.

answer: Together these goals aimed at building a strong, self-reliant and just economy.

questions.q: What was the Green Revolution, and what were its limitations?

answer.text: The Green Revolution refers to the large increase in the production of foodgrains, especially wheat and rice, that resulted from the use of high-yielding variety seeds, along with chemical fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation, from the mid-1960s. It made India self-sufficient in foodgrains and freed it from dependence on food imports.

However, the benefits were uneven. The gains were concentrated in a few prosperous regions such as Punjab and Haryana and mainly in wheat and rice, while other regions and crops lagged behind. The new inputs were costly, so rich farmers gained more than poor ones, widening inequality. There were also concerns about overuse of water and chemicals harming the soil and environment.

answer: Thus the Green Revolution brought food security but also created regional and social disparities.
